comments.text: I’m Puerto Rican, Puerto Rico is never going to be a state, and we never should. There’s way too many obstacles blocking it from happening that it’s near to impossible, and if somehow it did happen, it would be detrimental to both the US and Puerto Rico financially, politically, and culturally. Those referendums that say we want statehood are total BS, they are only setup by the extremely corrupt Pro-statehood party PNP just as political ploys to get their more ignorant and gullible voters out to vote for them in the elections. They are nonbinding referendums, meaning they were never approved by congress to happen in the first place, so congress isn’t mandated to take any action on the results, which is also why most Puerto Ricans who are against statehood boycott the referendums, because nothing will happen either way. The reason most Americans in the continental US are almost all unanimously push for statehood is because PNP has controlled the Resident Commissioner seat since the year 2000, so for 25 years they have been pushing this false narrative that the island unanimously wants statehood, and they disguise the statehood movement as a Civil Rights movement cause that’s what they know Americans will listen too. So, if you hear a Puerto Rican that is for statehood talk about it like it’s about “Civil Rights”, “Equality”, “Representation”, or “Our men and women fought in the uniform”, they are trying to get you to pity the island into statehood. When in reality, if you go to the island and ask the average statehooders off the street and listen to the PNP narrative on the island, to them its all about just getting more money to live off welfare to be lazy and section 8, and to the politicians it’s about more federal funds to steal cause the statehood politicians are extremely corrupt. But all in all, statehood support is declining on the island because of all the corruption being exposed in the statehood movement and neglect by the US government. Independence support is rising and even becoming mainstream in the news and pop culture on the island with even Puerto Rican celebrities calling for Puerto Rico to be free from the US.
